introduction_strategy.hook_hypothesis: Modern style transfer methods increasingly face a three-way tension among artistic strength, content fidelity, and computational efficiency. The introduction should motivate why efficient multi-style transfer remains important despite progress in arbitrary and diffusion-based style transfer.
introduction_strategy.problem_gap_hypothesis: Existing methods either rely on global statistics, attention/transformer mechanisms, heavy diffusion sampling, or efficient multi-style representations that can introduce artifacts. The gap is a reproducible latent-space method that provides competitive style-content trade-offs with explicit distribution matching and path regularization.

related_work_strategy.overview: Organize related work into classical and arbitrary neural style transfer, attention/transformer and multi-style transfer, diffusion or training-free style transfer, and optimal-transport/distributional objectives. Each cluster should identify why existing methods leave room for fast latent-space bridge-style transfer.

subsections.subsection_title: Classical and Arbitrary Neural Style Transfer
subsections.methodology_cluster: Gram statistics, normalization-based transfer, and feed-forward arbitrary style transfer.
subsections.sota_investigation_mission: Survey Gatys-style Gram matching, AdaIN, SANet, AesPA-Net, and AesFA as foundations for style/content decoupling and perceptual evaluation.
subsections.limitation_hypothesis: These methods can be fast or high-quality but often rely on image-space statistics or reference-image conditioning and do not explicitly model a latent transport path with terminal distribution matching.

subsections.bridge_to_our_method: The proposed method keeps the feed-forward efficiency goal but replaces direct statistic matching with latent bridge dynamics and terminal SWD.

subsections.methodology_cluster: Attention-based style transfer, transformer style transfer, and style-bank or style-representation approaches for many styles.
subsections.sota_investigation_mission: Cover StyTr2, S2WAT, SaMST, StyleBank-like multi-style mechanisms, and related efficient multi-style systems.
subsections.limitation_hypothesis: Attention and multi-style representations can preserve structure and scale to many styles, but may not explicitly regularize the transport path and may produce structured grain or washed artifacts.

subsections.bridge_to_our_method: The proposed style spatial prior and semantic cross-attention are kept lightweight but are embedded into a bridge objective with SWD and kinetic regularization.

subsections.methodology_cluster: Diffusion-based and training-free style transfer methods such as StyleID and CAST.
subsections.sota_investigation_mission: Investigate StyleID, CAST, and diffusion-style transfer lines as quality-oriented or training-free baselines.
subsections.limitation_hypothesis: These methods can yield strong style semantics but may suffer from semantic drift, high inference cost, or lower suitability for fast domain-level multi-style inference.
